Select the Optimal Biological Dose of BOIN-ET Trials

Source: R/boin_et_select_obd.R
boin_et_select_obd.Rd

Select the optimal biological dose (OBD) from the final data of one or more trials of the BOIN-ET design, with the estimators and selection rules of the 'boinet' package.

Usage

boin_et_select_obd(
  n_pts,
  n_tox,
  n_resp,
  target,
  target_resp,
  p_saf = NULL,
  p_tox = NULL,
  p_saf_resp = NULL,
  cutoff_eli = 0.95,
  cutoff_eli_resp = 0.99,
  p_eli = NULL,
  p_eli_resp = NULL,
  est_method = c("observed", "multi_iso", "fp_logistic"),
  obd_method = c("max_resp", "utility_weighted", "utility_truncated_linear",
    "utility_scoring"),
  w1 = 0.33,
  w2 = 1.09,
  t_low = NULL,
  t_upp = NULL,
  e_low = NULL,
  e_upp = NULL,
  psi00 = 40,
  psi11 = 60,
  early_stop = NULL,
  boinet_compatible = FALSE
)

Arguments

n_pts

Integer vector of patients treated at each dose, or a matrix with one row per trial.

n_tox

DLT counts of the same shape as n_pts.

n_resp

Response counts of the same shape as n_pts.

target

Numeric scalar. Target DLT probability, for example 0.30.

target_resp

Numeric scalar. Target response probability, for example 0.60.

p_saf

Numeric scalar. Highest DLT probability deemed subtherapeutic. Defaults to 0.1 * target, the value recommended by Takeda et al. (2018), which is far below the 0.6 * target of the BOIN design.

p_tox

Numeric scalar. Lowest DLT probability deemed overly toxic. Defaults to 1.4 * target.

p_saf_resp

Numeric scalar. Highest response probability deemed subtherapeutic. Defaults to 0.6 * target_resp.

cutoff_eli

Numeric scalar. A dose is no longer admissible when the posterior probability that its DLT rate is below p_eli falls below 1 - cutoff_eli. Defaults to 0.95.

cutoff_eli_resp

Numeric scalar. A dose is no longer admissible when the posterior probability that its response rate is above p_eli_resp falls below 1 - cutoff_eli_resp. Defaults to 0.99.

p_eli

Numeric scalar or NULL. DLT probability of the rule above. Defaults to NULL, which uses target as the 'boinet' package does. Takeda et al. (2018) used 0.40 with a cutoff of 0.90.

p_eli_resp

Numeric scalar or NULL. Response probability of the rule above. Defaults to NULL, which uses p_saf_resp as the 'boinet' package does. Takeda et al. (2018) used 0.20 with a cutoff of 0.90.

est_method

Character scalar. Estimator of the response rates: "observed" (the default) for the observed rates, "multi_iso" for the model-averaged unimodal isotonic regression of Lin and Yin (2017), or "fp_logistic" for the fractional polynomial logistic regression of Takeda et al. (2018), which needs the 'mfp' package.

obd_method

Character scalar. Selection rule: "max_resp" (the default) for the admissible dose with the highest estimated response rate up to the estimated MTD, or the dose that maximizes the utility "utility_weighted", "utility_truncated_linear" or "utility_scoring" among the admissible doses.

w1, w2

Numeric scalars. Weights of the weighted utility q - w1 * p - w2 * p * (p > p_tox), where p and q are the estimated DLT and response rates. Default to 0.33 and 1.09.

t_low, t_upp

Numeric scalars or NULL. DLT rates between which the truncated linear utility falls from one to zero. Default to p_saf and p_tox.

e_low, e_upp

Numeric scalars or NULL. Response rates between which the truncated linear utility rises from zero to one. Default to p_saf_resp / 2 and target_resp.

psi00, psi11

Numeric scalars. Scores of the scoring utility for a patient with neither DLT nor response and for a patient with both, the scores of a response without DLT and of a DLT without response being 100 and 0. Default to 40 and 60.

early_stop

Logical vector or NULL. TRUE for the trials stopped early, which select no OBD. Defaults to NULL, no early stop.

boinet_compatible

Logical scalar. Apply the rule of the 'boinet' package (version 1.6.0), in which a dose excluded by its DLT data does not exclude the doses above it. Defaults to FALSE; see Details.

Value

A list with components

obd

Integer vector of the selected dose levels, NA when no dose is selected.

reason

Character vector: "selected", "early_stop" or "no_admissible_dose".

probe

Numeric matrix of the response estimates, NA for the doses not tried.

Details

Only the doses with at least one patient are considered. A dose is admissible when the posterior probability that its DLT rate is below p_eli is at least 1 - cutoff_eli and the posterior probability that its response rate is above p_eli_resp is at least 1 - cutoff_eli_resp, under uniform priors, and when no lower dose is excluded by its DLT data. When no dose is admissible, no OBD is selected. Otherwise the DLT rates of the doses tried are estimated by isotonic regression of the observed rates with equal weights. Under "max_resp" the estimated MTD is the highest dose whose estimate is as close to target as that of the closest admissible dose, and the OBD is the admissible dose up to the MTD with the highest response estimate. Ties go to the lowest dose. These are the rules of boinet::obd.select(), except that in 'boinet' a dose excluded by its DLT data does not exclude the doses above it, which can then be selected; boinet_compatible = TRUE applies this rule, and boin_et_simulate explains the change.

The response estimates (under "max_resp") and the utilities are compared after rounding to ten decimals, and ties go to the lowest dose. Doses whose utilities are equal as fractions then tie whatever the rounding error of the platform. This happens regularly: with "utility_scoring" and its default scores, a dose with 1 DLT and 7 responses in 15 patients and a dose with 4 DLTs and 9 responses in 15 patients both have the utility 196 / 3. 'boinet' compares the utilities as computed, so that rounding error decides between such doses, and versions of this package up to 2.2.0 did the same; in these trials, a few in a thousand, the selected dose can therefore differ from that of boinet::obd.select() and from that of earlier versions, also with boinet_compatible = TRUE.

The model-based estimates are computed in R once for every distinct set of final data; the selection itself runs in C++.

References

Takeda, K., Taguri, M. and Morita, S. (2018). BOIN-ET: Bayesian optimal interval design for dose finding based on both efficacy and toxicity outcomes. Pharmaceutical Statistics, 17(4), 383-395. doi:10.1002/pst.1864

Yamaguchi, Y., Takeda, K., Yoshida, S. and Maruo, K. (2024). Optimal biological dose selection in dose-finding trials with model-assisted designs based on efficacy and toxicity: a simulation study. Journal of Biopharmaceutical Statistics, 34(3), 379-393. doi:10.1080/10543406.2023.2202259

Lin, R. and Yin, G. (2017). STEIN: A simple toxicity and efficacy interval design for seamless phase I/II clinical trials. Statistics in Medicine, 36(26), 4106-4120. doi:10.1002/sim.7428

See also

sim_boin_et, boin_et_simulate

Examples

# One trial: patients, DLTs and responses at four doses
boin_et_select_obd(
  n_pts = c(3, 6, 12, 3), n_tox = c(0, 1, 3, 2), n_resp = c(0, 2, 7, 2),
  target = 0.30, target_resp = 0.60
)
#> $obd
#> [1] 3
#> 
#> $reason
#> [1] "selected"
#> 
#> $probe
#>      DL1       DL2       DL3       DL4
#> [1,]   0 0.3333333 0.5833333 0.6666667
#> 

# The OBD under a utility
boin_et_select_obd(
  n_pts = c(3, 6, 12, 3), n_tox = c(0, 1, 3, 2), n_resp = c(0, 2, 7, 2),
  target = 0.30, target_resp = 0.60, obd_method = "utility_scoring"
)$obd
#> [1] 3
